rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 28 September 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 DBS Hong Kong says it will progressively introduce agentic capabilities for authenticated corporate and SME virtual-assistant users from 26 September; this is a market and control watch, not a new Hong Kong requirement. Hong Kong 🟡 DBS Hong Kong announces agentic virtual-assistant rollout for corporate and SME users 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260925-hk-banks-news-3ae09be694 ⏰ Deadline: Progressive Hong Kong introduction from 26 September 2026; later retail agentic phase planned for 2027 Products: Corporate digital banking, SME servicing, Payments DBS Hong Kong says it will progressively introduce agentic capabilities to DBS Joy for DBS IDEAL corporate and SME users from 26 September 2026. DBS says authenticated customers can complete supported banking tasks through conversation and that the assistant retrieves, analyses and presents transaction and account information. The release is an official product announcement, not a regulatory requirement or a finding of a control failure. Comparable digital servicing may warrant a market watch on task permissions, customer authorisation, account-data use, human escalation and operational support, while the release does not establish the underlying control design. Source: DBS Hong Kong’s Gen AI-enabled virtual assistants reach over 1 million customers and go agentic Mainland/GBA No validated current-run items. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. No validated current-run benchmark items. Watch List • Monitor the disclosed DBS rollout for supported task permissions and customer-authorisation arrangements; the announcement does not provide those details.
